children.topic: Etiology (TIGAR-O System)
Toxic-metabolic: Alcohol (70-80%), Smoking, Hypercalcemia, Hyperlipidemia, Chronic renal failure
Idiopathic: Early onset (juvenile) vs Late onset (senile)
Genetic: PRSS1 (hereditary pancreatitis, 50x cancer risk), SPINK1, CFTR mutations
Autoimmune: Type 1 (systemic IgG4-RD, sausage-shaped pancreas), Type 2 (pancreas-specific, GEL lesions)
Recurrent & Severe AP: Post-necrotic pancreatitis
Obstructive: Pancreas divisum, ductal stricture, tumor, trauma
Classic Clinical Triad & Features
Classic Triad: 1. Pancreatic Calcifications (on X-ray/CT) 2. Steatorrhea (exocrine failure) 3. Diabetes Mellitus (endocrine failure)
Abdominal Pain: Postprandial epigastric pain radiating to back, dull, constant, leads to opioid dependence and weight loss
Malabsorption: Fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies (A, D, E, K), weight loss despite good appetite
Diagnostic Workup
Fecal Elastase-1 (<200 µg/g = pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, <100 = severe): Best non-invasive screening test!
Abdominal CT: Duct dilation, intraductal calcifications, parenchymal atrophy
MRCP / Secretin-MRCP: Chain-of-lakes / ductal side-branching, early ductal changes
EUS: Rosemont criteria (hyperechoic foci, strands, lobularity, duct wall hyperechoic)
Surgical Management
Indications: Intractable pain (most common), complications (biliary/duodenal obstruction, pseudocyst, splenic vein thrombosis)
Ductal Drainage Procedures (Dilated Main Duct >6-7 mm):
Partington-Rochelle Procedure: Modified Puestow (longitudinal pancreaticojejunostomy Roux-en-Y)
Resectional & Hybrid Procedures (Inflammatory Head Mass / Small Duct):
Frey Procedure: Local excision of head of pancreas + longitudinal pancreaticojejunostomy (Hybrid)
Beger Procedure: Duodenum-preserving pancreatic head resection (DPPHR)
Whipple Procedure (Pancreaticoduodenectomy): Reserved for suspicion of malignancy
